core.title: Surface every DESIRED OUTCOME obligation in the flow router or declare a structural residual
core.given: A user/system flow flow router, the plan artifact that projects the user/system flow's DESIRED OUTCOME obligations, is the subject of CONFIRM validation.
core.when: CONFIRM checks that the flow router covers the DESIRED OUTCOME obligations it projects.
core.then: Every DESIRED OUTCOME obligation must surface in the flow router as a message, self-message, guard, fragment, or invariant, or be declared in it as an explicit structural residual.
prefer: For each DESIRED OUTCOME ref, either show it with one of the five surface kinds or list it as an explicit structural residual with a residual id that names the DESIRED OUTCOME ref.
Use the notation the project's flow router validator already recognises; copy the form of existing passing flow routers.
avoid: Leaving a DESIRED OUTCOME ref with neither a surface nor an explicit structural residual (silent omission).
Adding vague catch-all diagram elements that satisfy coverage without expressing the obligation.
core.why: The flow router is a projection that must cover its source DESIRED OUTCOME obligations; an obligation that neither surfaces nor is declared residual is silently lost from the user/system flow's behavioural contract.
evidence: The stack's coverage check for flow router DESIRED OUTCOME surface-or-residual passes at CONFIRM.
For each failure the report identifies the flow router, the DESIRED OUTCOME ref concerned, its surface kind, its residual id, and the coverage status.
verification: Coverage check: the flow router is a projection of its source DESIRED OUTCOME obligations; every DESIRED OUTCOME ref must have an accepted surface or an explicit structural residual in the flow router.
Accepted surface kinds are exactly message, self-message, guard, fragment and invariant; a DESIRED OUTCOME ref carried any other way requires an explicit structural residual.
Enforced at the CONFIRM phase with confirm-blocking enforcement: a failure blocks CONFIRM. The current phase must be supplied by the harness (needs a new observer).
The check runs on every flow router validated at CONFIRM, whether or not the planner authored or edited it in this task.
Only artifacts whose subject kind is flow router are subjects; standalone product capability or DESIRED OUTCOME documents and sequence diagrams that are not flow routers are out of scope.
Each failure reports the flow router id, the DESIRED OUTCOME ref, the surface kind, the residual id and the coverage status.
Severity 4, disposition strict: findings are enforced, not advisory.

fires: CONFIRM validates a flow router that the planner authored or edited in this task.
CONFIRM validates an existing, unchanged flow router (the coverage check runs regardless of whether the flow router changed).
doesNotFire: Any phase other than CONFIRM (a planner may check coverage early while drafting, but the rule's enforcement point is CONFIRM).
Artifacts whose subject kind is not flow router, such as a standalone product capability or DESIRED OUTCOME document or a sequence diagram that is not a flow router.

neutralityNotes: This rule governs ATDD planner plan artifacts (user/system flow, flow router, DESIRED OUTCOME) at the CONFIRM phase; that vocabulary is method-level and identical across stack realizations, so it stays in the core, which names no stack, runtime, framework, language, package manager, file suffix or path. The five surface kinds (message, self-message, guard, fragment, invariant) are the flow router artifact's own notation and part of the convention's canonical statement rather than stack machinery, so they are kept in the core instead of being pushed to a (non-existent) profile key; a stack whose flow router notation differed would surface that through its plan-artifact kinds. Validator id, validation-registry ids (family/template/variant) and the finding-field schema of this one rule are Bun-only. Severity and disposition remain rule-local verification. The only profile dependency is the identification of flow router and DESIRED OUTCOME as the stack's plan-artifact kinds (roles.plan_artifact.kinds).
